messages:
maria: Quick async check — I'm proposing a tiny API contract change for routing hints. Want to validate compatibility and canary plan before I open the PR.

maria: Current behavior: POST /v1/generate accepts optional routing_hint (string) with these values: "region:us", "region:eu", "tier:premium", "fallback:compatible". If omitted we use user default region + best-effort model selection.

maria: Proposal: allow multiple routing hints in an array (routing_hints: [string]) and add a new hint "latency-sensitive" which prefers low-latency shards. Also tighten fallback semantics: fallback_policy becomes explicit (one of "none", "compatible", "downgrade").

aj: :eyes: That seems reasonable but need to confirm backward compat for clients that send a single string. Do we accept both string and array?

maria: Yes — server will accept either string or array for 12w. We'll return a Deprecation-Warning header if string is used. Then remove string support after evergreen notice window.

sanjay: Two quick notes: 1) Make sure SDKs parse both shapes. 2) Add a compatibility header in responses so downstream routers can log which hint resolved (e.g., X-Routing-Resolved: region=eu;model=redwood-14b-q4).

tay: +1 on the header. Also, is "latency-sensitive" transitive with "tier:premium"? i.e., if they give both, which wins?

maria: Priority order: explicit model_id > specific tier/regional hint pair > generic hints like latency-sensitive. We'll document priority and implement in routing code. Example: ["region:us","tier:premium","latency-sensitive"] => prefer premium in us, then pick latency-optimized shard.

liam: For rollback/fallback behavior: what does "downgrade" mean? Return lower-capability model or 503?

maria: "downgrade" = serve a compatible lower-capacity model variant (same family) and set X-Routing-Resolved with model and a warning code. "none" = fail fast with 503. "compatible" = try compatible family models then downgrade if none match.

aj: Tests to add: unit tests for parsing string vs array, integration test that Deprecation-Warning is emitted for string, e2e for priority ordering, and an observability test that X-Routing-Resolved shows accurate model metadata.

sanjay: Also add a lint rule in api-contract-check to reject new hint values without a corresponding enum update in docs. We had a regression last quarter where a new hint leaked without docs.

maria: Good call — I'll add the lint entry. Will draft the PR with changes to: runtime routing module, contract proto, SDK parsers, and API docs. Plan: canary 10% of requests for 72h, metrics: error rate, p95 latency, model downgrade rate, and docs link coverage.

tay: For canary buckets — prefer internal org only for first 24h then public 10%? Can we do org-scoped canary?

maria: We have support for org-scoped routing via feature flags. Canary step plan: 1) internal orgs 100% for 24h 2) public 10% for 72h 3) rollout 100% if no regressions. I'll include explicit kill-switch in rollout job.

liam: Ping me on the PR for review. I'll specifically check rollback behavior and tests for the header.

aj: I can add SDK changes once API surface is in a draft spec.

maria: Thanks. I'll open PR later today and link RFC + smoke job. Example request shape I'll include in PR:

```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model_id": "redwood-14b-q4",
  "input": "Summarize...",
  "routing_hints": ["region:us", "tier:premium", "latency-sensitive"],
  "fallback_policy": "compatible"
}
```

maria: Response will include: X-Routing-Resolved header and Deprecation-Warning if client used string routing_hint.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/routing-hint-v2 -> start at 2026-05-04T17:00Z (placeholder)

sanjay: If anyone is blocked on docs or examples, tag me. Also we should add a migration guide snippet for third-party clients.

maria: Will do. Thanks everyone — will post PR link and checklist in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
